name: Skyline Queenstown
bio: A gondola up Bob's Peak to the classic view over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables, with luge tracks at the top.

name: Kawarau Gorge Suspension Bridge
bio: The 1880 bridge where AJ Hackett launched the world's first commercial bungy jump, 43 m above the river.

name: Shotover Jet
bio: A high-speed jet boat that spins and skims past the rock walls of the narrow Shotover River canyons.

name: Walter Peak High Country Farm
bio: A high-country sheep station across Lake Wakatipu, reached by the TSS Earnslaw, with a homestead serving lunch and dinner.

name: Arrowtown
bio: A gold-rush village of heritage cottages and a restored Chinese miners' settlement, ablaze with colour in autumn.

name: Ben Lomond Track
bio: A big climb from the top of the gondola to a 1,748 m summit with views across the lake and the Southern Alps.

name: Queenstown Gardens
bio: A lakeside peninsula of lawns, rose beds and a frisbee-golf course, with the Remarkables framed across the water.

name: Gibbston Valley
bio: A narrow river valley of Pinot Noir vineyards, with cellar doors and a wine cave carved into the hillside.

name: Coronet Peak
bio: A ski field on the slopes of a 1,649 m peak above Arrowtown, the closest to Queenstown at about 20 minutes by road.

name: The Remarkables
bio: A jagged range rising from Lake Wakatipu's south-east shore, with a ski area and a walk to Lake Alta.

name: Lake Hayes
bio: A small lake in the Wakatipu Basin, circled by a walking and cycling track that is part of the Queenstown Trail and popular for swimming.

name: Skippers Canyon
bio: A 22 km gorge carved by the Shotover River, an old gold-mining area reached by a narrow gravel road above sheer drops.

name: Arrowtown Chinese Settlement
bio: Stone huts built by Chinese gold miners in the 1860s on Bush Creek, a short walk from Arrowtown's main street.

name: Queenstown Trail
bio: Cycling and walking trails linking Queenstown with Arrowtown, Jack's Point and Gibbston, beside rivers and lakes.

name: That Wānaka Tree
bio: A lone willow growing out of Lake Wānaka, at its most magical at dawn with the mountains reflected behind it.

name: Roys Peak
bio: A steep, exposed climb to a ridge with the famous view over Lake Wānaka and Mount Aspiring. Closed 1 Oct – 10 Nov.

name: Puzzling World
bio: A leaning clock tower, a two-storey maze and rooms of mind-bending optical illusions.

name: Mount Iron
bio: A short climb over a glacier-carved knoll to a summit overlooking the town, the lake and the Clutha River.

name: Cardrona Hotel
bio: An 1863 gold-rush hotel on the Crown Range road, one of the oldest in New Zealand, with a sunny garden bar.

name: Dunedin Railway Station
bio: A Flemish Renaissance gem of basalt and limestone, with a mosaic-floored hall — New Zealand's most photographed building.

name: Larnach Castle
bio: A Gothic Revival mansion high on the Otago Peninsula, with lavish interiors and celebrated gardens.

name: Royal Albatross Centre
bio: At Taiaroa Head, a hide overlooks the world's only mainland breeding colony of northern royal albatross.

name: Penguin Place
bio: A conservation reserve where trenches and hides bring you close to endangered yellow-eyed penguins.

name: Otago Museum
bio: Natural history, Pacific and Māori cultures, a tropical butterfly house and a planetarium beside the university.

name: Toitū Otago Settlers Museum
bio: The story of Otago told through Māori, Scottish and Chinese settlers, vintage trams and a hall of portraits.

name: Baldwin Street
bio: A short residential street so steep it has held the title of the world's steepest — walk up if you dare.

name: Tunnel Beach
bio: Sandstone sea arches and a hand-carved Victorian tunnel leading down to a hidden cove.

name: Sandfly Bay
bio: Giant sand dunes tumble down to a wild beach where New Zealand sea lions often doze on the sand.

name: Oamaru Blue Penguin Colony
bio: From a grandstand at dusk, watch rafts of little blue penguins — the world's smallest — come ashore and waddle home.

name: Oamaru Victorian Precinct
bio: Grand whitestone warehouses and banks from the 1870s, now filled with craftspeople, booksellers and bars.

name: Steampunk HQ
bio: A clanking, smoking museum of retro-futurist machines, with a steam locomotive and a mirrored infinity room.

name: Moeraki Boulders
bio: Huge, almost perfectly spherical boulders scattered along Koekohe Beach, formed over millions of years.

name: Bushy Beach
bio: A clifftop hide above a beach where rare yellow-eyed penguins come ashore in the late afternoon.

name: Nugget Point
bio: A lighthouse on a knife-edge headland above a scatter of rocky islets, with fur seals below.

name: Purakaunui Falls
bio: A graceful three-tiered waterfall reached by a short walk through podocarp forest.

name: Cathedral Caves
bio: Vast sea caves 30 m high on Waipati Beach, only reachable for a couple of hours either side of low tide.

name: McLean Falls
bio: The tallest waterfall in the Catlins, cascading 22 m through lush rainforest.

name: Curio Bay
bio: A 180-million-year-old petrified forest revealed at low tide, with yellow-eyed penguins and Hector's dolphins nearby.

name: Slope Point
bio: The southernmost point of the South Island, marked by a signpost amid wind-sculpted, sideways-growing trees.

name: Rob Roy Glacier Track
bio: A walk up a beech-forested valley in Mount Aspiring National Park to a hanging glacier spilling waterfalls.

name: Blue Pools
bio: Clear, glacier-blue pools in a beech forest gorge on the Haast Pass road, reached over swing bridges.

name: Haast Pass
bio: The alpine road pass between Wānaka and the West Coast, with waterfalls and short bush walks beside the highway.

name: Otago Central Rail Trail
bio: 152 km of gentle cycling along an old railway line through tunnels, viaducts and gold-rush villages.

name: Clyde
bio: A charming gold-rush town of stone cottages and old hotels beneath the Clyde Dam, at the start of the Rail Trail.

name: Blue Lake
bio: A vivid blue lake filling an old gold-sluicing pit, ringed by eroded white cliffs beside a tiny historic village.

name: Cromwell Heritage Precinct
bio: Old Cromwell rebuilt stone by stone on the shore of Lake Dunstan after the town was flooded by the Clyde Dam.

name: Glenorchy
bio: A tiny village at the head of Lake Wakatipu, beneath the peaks and valleys used as Middle-earth in The Lord of the Rings.
